Meta-analysis of within-subject variability in published bioequivalence studies

INTERIM read-out — data extraction in progress

Jerry Hu

2026-06-02

INTERIM read-out — data extraction in progress.

Interim status (2026-06-02). This is a preliminary read-out built while data extraction is still being conducted. Currently, the pooled estimates below consist of 15 studies. The target is 100–200 studies. After data extraction is complete, the datasets will be examined. Based on what data is available, the research objectives will be specified. In the meantime, descriptive statistics of the available data are reported below.

1 Background & objective

A bioequivalence (BE) study is powered on a CVw assumed in advance — guessed from a pilot, a prior study, or the literature. The within-subject CV drives the sample size of a 2×2 crossover directly: too low an assumption and the study is under-powered; too high and it is wastefully large. Once the study reads out, the realized CVw is whatever the data deliver.

Question. Across the published BE record, how does the assumed CVw compare to the realized CVw, and how does that gap move the BE outcome — the geometric mean ratio (GMR) point estimate, the 90% CI width, and realized vs planned power? Because absolute CVw is drug-specific, the poolable quantity is the dimensionless observed/assumed ratio \(r = \mathrm{CV_w^{obs}} / \mathrm{CV_w^{assumed}}\).

2 Methods

2.1 Data sources & literature search

Data are collected from the published bioequivalence record by a PRISMA-aligned systematic search, framed as an open search-term census over the modern reporting era (2010–present) and run to exhaustion: a fixed Boolean query is applied across the searchable corpora and every eligible record is included (no convenience cut; a pre-specified random sample, seed 20260601, is the only down-selection if the eligible pool ever exceeds extraction capacity).

  • Corpora. Peer-reviewed publications via PubMed / PMC (open-access full text) and the EMA EPAR repository; FDA review packages are retrieved by product as a supplementary stream (Drugs@FDA has no study-level search interface). The current census has identified 1,675 PubMed records, 212 EMA EPARs, and 2 FDA seed records (1,887 total).
  • Query. bioequivalence / bioequivalent AND crossover / replicate AND Cmax / AUC / “90% confidence interval” AND “sample size” / “intra-subject coefficient of variation” (logged verbatim in stage 01-search).
  • Screening (two-phase). A title/abstract pass (agent-assisted, high volume) followed by full-text eligibility on the survivors.
  • Inclusion. Human, single-dose (or clearly-reported steady-state) BE study; test vs reference of a defined formulation; 2×2 crossover or replicate / RSABE design; reports n and a 90% CI for at least one PK metric (or, for highly-variable drugs, a directly-reported replicate-ANOVA CVw).
  • Exclusion. Parallel-design studies; population / individual-BE only; in-vitro / dissolution-only; narrative reviews; and any record with no usable 90% CI, no directly-reported CVw, and no interpretable n (nothing to derive from). Records appearing in more than one source (journal, EPAR, FDA review) are de-duplicated to a single study, preferring the most complete source.
  • AI-readable-only analysis set. Only records whose full text is machine-retrievable are extracted — there is no human-fetch of paywalled articles. This is a deliberate scope decision (access, not topic, is the binding constraint) and a stated coverage limitation: the analyzed set is biased toward open-access reporting. Of the PubMed records that advanced to full-text, 301 have retrievable open full text (the extraction denominator); 108 have been extracted so far in this interim cut.

2.2 Per-study extraction

We extract, per study, the reported design (n, α, planned GMR, target power), the planning CVw where stated, and the realized 90% CI of the GMR for each PK metric (Cmax, AUC0-t, AUC0-inf). From these we recover three quantities.

2.3 Realized CVw — back-calculated from n and the 90% CI

For a 2×2 crossover, the realized within-subject variance is recovered from the log-scale 90% CI half-width \(H\) of the GMR on \(n\) completers:

\[ \mathrm{SE} = \frac{H}{t_{0.95,\,n-2}}, \qquad \mathrm{MSE} = \mathrm{SE}^2 \cdot \frac{n}{2}, \qquad \mathrm{CV_w^{obs}} = \sqrt{e^{\mathrm{MSE}} - 1} \]

where \(H\) is the half-width of the CI on the log ratio, \(t_{0.95,\,n-2}\) the upper 5% Student-\(t\) quantile on \(n-2\) degrees of freedom, \(\mathrm{SE}\) the standard error of the treatment difference on the log scale, and \(\mathrm{MSE}\) the residual (within-subject) mean square. This back-calculation is validated against the subset of studies that report the ANOVA CVw directly (agreement reported in the full read-out).

2.4 Assumed CVw — stated, or inverted from the chosen n

Where the sample-size justification states the planning CVw, it is used directly. Otherwise it is recovered by inverting the 2×2 sample-size relation for the CVw that makes the chosen \(n\) exactly adequate under the study’s stated GMR, α, and target power:

\[ n \;=\; \text{ssize}_{2\times2}\!\left(\mathrm{CV_w^{assumed}},\, \mathrm{GMR},\, \alpha,\, 1-\beta\right) \;\;\Longrightarrow\;\; \mathrm{CV_w^{assumed}} = \text{solve for the CV at the chosen } n \]

the inversion uses the conventional two one-sided-tests (TOST) sample-size function (PowerTOST); the recovered value is validated on studies that state the planning CV explicitly. This interim read-out pools only the directly-stated planning CVs; the inverted set is validated but not yet folded into the headline.

2.5 Planning gap and its consequence

\[ r = \frac{\mathrm{CV_w^{obs}}}{\mathrm{CV_w^{assumed}}}, \qquad \text{realized power} = \text{power}_\text{TOST}\!\left(\mathrm{CV} = \mathrm{CV_w^{obs}},\; n = n_\text{total},\; \mathrm{GMR},\; \alpha\right) \]

\(r > 1\) means the study realized more variability than it planned for (under-planned, power eroded); \(r < 1\) means it planned conservatively. Realized power re-evaluates the TOST power at the CV the data actually delivered, holding n and the planned GMR fixed.

3 Results

3.1 Before vs after: assumed vs realized CVw

Each row is one study-metric: the grey dot is the assumed (planning) CVw, the coloured dot the realized CVw; red marks studies where the realized CV exceeded what was planned for.

The ratio collapses this to one dimensionless number per comparison:

  • Central tendency: the geometric-mean ratio is 0.962 (IQR 0.803–1.23), i.e. planning CVw is on average close to realized — but the spread is wide (range 0.29–2.63).
  • Direction: in 44.4% of comparisons the realized CVw exceeded the assumed value — the under-planned tail that erodes power.

BE pass rate 85.2%
Note: Interim: 15 studies / 27 PK-metric comparisons of 108 papers extracted. Descriptive pooling (geometric mean), not inverse-variance weighted.

The planned GMR is 1.1 ( 110%) — the canonical sample-size assumption — against a realized GMR of 1.01 ( 101%) at the median. Although the median realized power ( 96%) sits above target, 37% of comparisons fall below 80% once re-evaluated at the realized CVw — the practical cost of the planning gap.

4 Interim limitations

  • Small analyzable N. Only studies that state a planning CVw enter the pooled estimate at this stage; assumed-CV recovery by inversion (which roughly triples the set) is validated but not yet folded into the headline. Estimates will shift.
  • Descriptive pooling. No inverse-variance weighting or between-study heterogeneity model yet (deferred to 04-analyze); each comparison counts equally.
  • Image-locked tables and non-2×2 designs are excluded here; selection toward cleanly-reported studies is possible.
  • Method label provisional. Whether the hierarchical “MBMA” layer materializes is a post-extraction decision; the slug may be renamed ma- before final publish.

5 Reproducibility

Pipeline (run in order): 01-search → 02-extract → 03-derive/normalize_derive.R → 05-tlf/build_tlf.R → this report. Seed 20260601. Back-calculation and TOST power use PowerTOST. This interim read-out was built from 108 extracted papers as of 2026-06-02.
